Master Lecture · Fashion image analysis

Two passes: evidence → analysis

Pass 1 · Formal evidence

Dot → line → plane → shape → form → colour → composition → space.

Pass 2 · Critical reading

Describe → inventory → origin → production → meaning → power → circulation.

Do not jump from impression to message. Evidence first; then claim.

Master Lecture · Fashion image analysis

1 · Describe before you interpret

Say what is there: bodies, clothes, light, text, crop. Not yet what it means.

Start with observable evidence; postpone the message.

2 · Language ≠ medium ≠ support

Separate code, channel or genre, and material or file.

Do not call the screen the medium when you mean the JPEG.

3 · The photo organises fashion

The image is not decoration: it charts fashion’s discursive space.

Photographic images play a key role in defining global fashion culture and in charting its discursive space.

(Shinkle 2008, 14)

Master Lecture · Fashion image analysis

4 · No single genre

Editorial, advertising, beauty, documentary: do not use one method for all.

there is no single and easily described genre of 'fashion photography'. Equally, there is no single methodology which is best suited to its analysis

(Shinkle 2008, 17)

5 · Agency, reception, experience

Circulation is not only views: who acts, who receives, what is felt?

The question of dramaturgy has been expanded to include aspects of agency, reception and experience within its purview.

(Eckersall 2017, 219)

Master Lecture · Fashion image analysis

Recall check

Alone, from memory, 3 minutes. Then compare with a partner.

  1. Kandinsky: point, line, plane — looking order or total geometry claim?
  2. Name the first three steps of the morphological chain.
  3. Shinkle 2008, 17: single genre/method?
  4. Which step must appear or the analysis card fails?
  5. Eckersall 2017 is pinned here for agency in what?

Course geometric background · threshold · #c378606cc29b · Original course SVG

Timer: 3 minutes. Students answer alone, from memory, on paper; no notes, no slides.

Then 2 minutes in pairs: compare answers, then check the lesson.

Practice only: nothing is collected or graded. Five more questions with answers are on the unit practice quiz page.

Answers:

  • 1. Looking order for attention/relation — not that every image is geometric (Kandinsky 2012, 9).
  • 2. Dot → line → plane (then shape, form, colour, composition, space).
  • 3. No single genre, no single method (Shinkle 2008, 17).
  • 4. Step 7 critical — description alone is not analysis.
  • 5. Reception / how meaning is negotiated in reception (Eckersall 2017, 219).

Ask: Which answer could you not recall? Re-read that idea before the Lab.
